newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures set for choppy range-trade.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures set for choppy range-trade.

text.p: German Bunds and futures appear set for a session of choppy range trade on Thursday after September Bund futures reached a new contract high on Wednesday as the market became unsettled by mark weakness.
At 0730 GMT, DTB September Bund futures were up two basis points at 103.27.
"I'm not looking for much movement today," said one Frankfurt dealer. "I would expect futures to stay within a range but for the market to be choppy."
Dealings will also take on a technical tone as traders looked for September futures to fil a gap near 103.10.

"The short-term outlook here is favoured to see a gap refilling back to 103.10. The 103 barrier could be tough to break in the current positive market tone," said MMS International in a market commentary.
MMS also said key intraday resistance is at 103.35, a point shy of the session high so far at 103.34.

Traders also said ongoing strength in the mark, which was trading above 1.82 marks in morning European dealings, could possibly weigh on the market amid fears the Bundesbank may be forced in the near-term to raise rates to defend the currency.
The bank's council meets on Thursday but no economists surveyed by Reuters expect a rate rise, even after data from three west German states on Wednesday showed higher inflation.

"If the mark were to continue its relentless trend lower, then such a sell-off cannot be completely ruled out, particularly if U.S. Treasuries were to weaken at the same time," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Futures & Options said.

"Such a situation would undoubtedly pull Bunds lower short-term as well without doing any damage to the longer-term bullish prospects," Deutsche said, noting any drop would represent another buying opportunity.
The German market on Thursday will take its cue from the U.S. market, which will focus on the release at 1230 GMT of weekly jobless claims, in the absence of fresh domestic economic data.
